subject.title: clawhub install does not register skill hooks automatically

question: What consent and trust policy should apply when an installed skill contains an executable OpenClaw hook pack?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing activation, but repository direction requires risky execution to remain explicit and operator-controlled; code alone cannot decide whether installation should prompt, remain download-only, or require a different package type.

options.title: Prompt Before Activation
options.body: Detect and scan hook packs, show their events and executable entrypoints, then require explicit confirmation before OpenClaw installs and enables them.

options.title: Download And Warn
options.body: Keep skill installation non-executing and emit a prominent warning with a supported explicit OpenClaw activation command.

options.title: Require Plugin Packaging
options.body: Reject executable hook packs inside ordinary skills and require authors to publish them as bundle or code-plugin packages with declared capabilities.

recommendation.title: Prompt Before Activation
recommendation.body: Detect and scan hook packs, show their events and executable entrypoints, then require explicit confirmation before OpenClaw installs and enables them.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses OpenClaw plugin installation, setup UX, and the security policy reflected in VISION.md.
